claim.quote: An excess of events is observed above the expected background, with a local significance of 5.0 standard deviations, at a mass near 125 GeV, signalling the production of a new particle.

date.note: A16: CMS announced the result in a joint CERN/ICHEP 2012 seminar on 4 July 2012, before the arXiv preprint (2012-07-31) or the Phys. Lett. B publication; the announcement date is used per A16.
date.quote: In a joint seminar today at CERN and the "ICHEP 2012" conference in Melbourne, CMS Experiment, CERN 4 July 2012

key_value.quote: a fit to these signals gives a mass of 125.3 +/- 0.4 (stat.) +/- 0.5 (syst.) GeV

name: Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV
notes: The collaboration wording is "observation of a new boson", not "discovery of the Higgs boson"; the identification with the standard model Higgs boson came later.

significance.quote: a local significance of 5.0 standard deviations

summary.plain: CMS found a new particle weighing about 125 times as much as a proton, the last missing piece of the standard model of particle physics. ATLAS announced the same discovery on the same day.
summary.technical: Combined search in the gamma gamma, ZZ, WW, tau tau and bb channels using up to 5.1 fb^-1 at 7 TeV and 5.3 fb^-1 at 8 TeV; local significance 5.0 sigma at m = 125.3 +/- 0.4 (stat.) +/- 0.5 (syst.) GeV.

title: Observation of a new boson at a mass of 125 GeV with the CMS experiment at the LHC
why_it_matters: The Higgs boson is the particle associated with the field that gives elementary particles their masses; its observation completed the standard model and opened a new field of precision Higgs measurements.
